SPOT_CASES.explanation: Has an input, a defined expected reference, AND an explicit, checkable criterion (specific keywords the summary must contain). Fully usable as-is.

SPOT_CASES.code:
{ input: "Ticket: \"Billing page shows wrong currency for EU customers\"",
  expected: "(judge if the summary is good)" }
SPOT_CASES.explanation: Has an input but no explicit, checkable criterion, just an implicit request to judge quality. Different reviewers (or the same reviewer on different days) would score this inconsistently. Needs a defined check before it's usable.
Exact-match criterion, appropriate here since a short ticket summary has a clear, narrow correct form. Fully usable and fully deterministic.

SPOT_CASES.code: { input: "Ticket: \"Password reset email never arrives, tried 3 times\"" }
SPOT_CASES.explanation: No expected output and no check function at all, there's nothing here to score against. This is just an input with no criterion, not a usable test case yet.

decision.t: A. Ship it, 96% beats the 91% baseline, that's a measurable win
decision.why: The 96% is real, but it's an average across a set where charge-disputes are only 2 of 50 cases, barely enough to move the aggregate even if the new prompt fails them completely. The number went up while a specific, high-stakes category quietly got much worse, exactly the "good average hides a catastrophic slice" failure this module warns about.

decision.t: B. Don't ship yet. Add real charge-dispute cases to the eval set, re-run, and check that slice specifically before deciding
decision.why: This is the correct move: the spot-check surfaced a real signal (4 of 5 wrong on a high-stakes category) that the eval set was underrepresenting. Before shipping, expand the eval set with enough charge-dispute cases to measure that slice properly, then compare THAT number to baseline, not just the aggregate. A category tied to money and disputes is exactly the kind of failure an average can hide and a slice can catch.

decision.t: C. Trust the manual spot-check over the eval suite entirely, and abandon the eval process for this decision
decision.why: The spot-check is valuable because it's what CAUGHT the gap, but 5 cases is too small a sample to replace a systematic eval on its own. The right response is to fold that signal back into a bigger, more representative eval set, not to throw out systematic measurement in favor of an ad hoc check, that's the exact anti-pattern this module opened by rejecting.

decision.t: D. Ship it, but plan to monitor charge-dispute complaints after launch
decision.why: Charge disputes are exactly the category where "monitor after shipping" is the expensive way to find out, real users would experience the 4-in-5 failure rate the spot-check already revealed. The eval gap is fixable before shipping; waiting for complaints just moves the cost onto users.
